browse.auth.no_source_access.description: Reason line on Who's watching when the profile was picked and every server that was reached refused it (HTTP 401): this profile genuinely has no grant on the server. Only for that case: a server that did not answer uses servers_unreachable and a certificate this TV does not trust uses tls_untrusted, so do not word this as a connection problem. {profile} is the profile's name. The picker draws it as one centred line.

browse.auth.tls_untrusted.value: Questo televisore non considera affidabile il certificato di sicurezza del tuo server. Aggiorna PlxNative e riprova.
browse.auth.tls_untrusted.description: Reason line on Who's watching or the sign-in read-out when the server answered over HTTPS but its certificate chain could not be verified against this television's trusted certificate authorities (X509 verify result 2, 18, 19, 20 or 21); it is NOT the wrong-clock case, which has its own line. The sentence names the remedy that exists in the app: results 2, 20 and 21 on a plex.direct name mean an out-of-date certificate store, which an update answers with newer bundled public roots; 18 and 19 mean the server presented its own root, which only the server's owner can fix. No placeholders. Sits in a two-line reason slot on the sign-in read-out and one centred line on the picker; keep the whole sentence at 125 characters or fewer.

browse.clock.notice_year.description: System toast shown once per app run when the app had to recognise the Plex server by its remembered key because the server's certificate failed its date check (most likely because the television's clock is wrong, but an expired certificate on a correct clock engages it too). Hedged on purpose ("looks wrong"): the app cannot know the clock is the cause. {year} is the four-digit year the television believes it is, written as plain digits. The toast wraps at roughly 40 characters per line and shows up to three lines, so keep the whole sentence at 120 characters or fewer and hedge it in every language.

browse.clock.notice.value: L'orologio della TV sembra errato. Connessione stabilita tramite la chiave memorizzata.
browse.clock.notice.description: Same toast as the year variant, for when the television's year is unknown. Keep it at 120 characters or fewer (up to three lines of roughly 40) and hedge it in every language.

browse.clock.no_key.value: L'orologio di questa TV sembra errato. Collega la TV a Internet una volta, poi riprova.
browse.clock.no_key.description: Reason line under the failed Home or Library read-out when the Plex server's certificate failed its date check and the app holds no remembered key for that server, so a wrong television clock is the likely cause. Hedged on purpose ("looks wrong"): the app cannot know the clock is the cause. Sits in a slot that shows two lines of about 70 characters each; keep the whole sentence under 140 characters.

browse.clock.key_changed.value: La chiave del tuo server è cambiata. Collega la TV a Internet una volta per consentire all'app di verificarla di nuovo.
browse.clock.key_changed.description: Reason line under the failed Home or Library read-out when the Plex server presented a different key than the one the app remembered, so the app will not trust it while the television's clock cannot be checked. Same two-line slot as the no-key line; keep the whole sentence under 140 characters.
